data.title: bn-1wv: Prototype an inspectable Lua ECS with a bullet-hell cart
data.description: Review deterministic Lua ECS semantics and bounds, protected ecs_query inspector/RPC, Radiant Swarm vertical slice, native/WASM/browser regressions, and documentation/skill completeness. web/engine.js is generated; source and parity tests remain in diff.

data.body: INFO: The 'matched' field counts every matching entity in the world, including those at or before the 'after' cursor, so it stays constant across pages while 'returned' shrinks. This is intentional and tested (tests/ecs.rs:201 asserts matched=5 on page 1 of 5) and useful as a world-total, but a caller paginating could misread it as 'remaining'. Worth a one-line note beside next_after in SPEC/skill docs. No change required.

data.reason: Reviewed the full ECS/RPC/game prototype against workspace source. Clean clippy; all tests pass (console-core ecs 4, dispatch 12, radiant_swarm 3, sprite 32). Verified: (1) ecs_query bounds validated defense-in-depth on both the Rust RPC layer (rpc.rs limit/with/select/fields/name checks) and the Lua inspector, with consistent limits and name grammar across both; (2) inspector protected via registry retention — a cart nulling the 'ecs' global cannot disable host inspection, and unselected component fields are provably not leaked (secret field test); (3) determinism via creation-order iteration and id-based pagination, with structural edits deferred during world:each and correctly flushed on callback error; (4) capacity, component-breadth, and MAX_SAFE_ID bounds enforced and tested. web/engine.js correctly gitignored as a generated artifact. No CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM issues; one INFO note on the 'matched' pagination semantic.

Accepted. matched is intentionally the total matching population across all pages; returned is the page count and next_after advances the cursor. The API references list these separately, and a future wording-only docs pass can make the distinction even more explicit.
